fact: Grant besieged Vicksburg after failed direct assaults on the city's defenses
source: Vicksburg: The Campaign That Opened the Mississippi, Michael B. Ballard (2004)

fact: Civilians dug caves into the hillside to shelter from Union shelling
source: My Cave Life in Vicksburg, Mary Ann Loughborough (1864)

fact: Residents resorted to eating mules, rats, and bread made from ground corn cobs and wallpaper paste
source: A Journal of the Siege of Vicksburg, anonymous diary published in various Civil War collections; also documented in Vicksburg: A People at War, 1860–1865, Gordon A. Cotton (1988)

fact: Confederate commander Pemberton surrendered Vicksburg on July 4, 1863
source: National Park Service — Vicksburg National Military Park

fact: Vicksburg did not officially celebrate the Fourth of July for approximately 81 years, until 1945
source: Widely documented local tradition; discussed in multiple sources including the Vicksburg Convention & Visitors Bureau and various histories. The exact duration (81 years) is sometimes cited as approximate, with the first official city-sponsored celebration occurring in 1945.
